description:
ARTHUR Phase 2 — Final Adversarial Audit Report
Scope: D:\A.R.T.H.U.R (current state; no git repo, so no diff/history review possible) against ARTHUR_Phase_2_Memory_RAG_DeepSeek_Implementation_Spec_v1.0. Review-only: zero source modifications; all probes used temp dirs under data\audit-* and :memory: DBs, cleaned up. Independent reproduction: npm run typecheck ✓, npm run build ✓, npm test 182 pass / 0 fail / 1 skip (live DeepSeek contract), npm run test:integration 51/51 pass — all re-run by me, all green.

1. Executive Verdict
PASS WITH FIXES
No BLOCKERs and no HIGHs. The isolation North Star holds end-to-end with direct evidence. Three MEDIUM findings (none cross-domain): JSON-shaped secrets bypass the secret gate, replay-after-forget resurrects a DELETED tombstone as a "success" (new text silently dropped), and a same-process crash-resume window leaves an ACTIVE item permanently unsearchable until restart. The rest are LOW polish/robustness items. All findings are localized, bounded, and fixable without changing the isolation architecture.

2. North Star Verdict
ISOLATION VERIFIED
Rule tested: only trusted server-side session state may select the Personal vs Business store; no fallback to Personal for invalid/missing sessions; no realistic cross-domain read/write/delete/ingest path exists.

Concrete evidence:

Single boundary, exhaustive branches. Grep over all of src/ shows exactly two store construction sites (src/app.ts:128-129, named PersonalMemoryStore/BusinessMemoryStore handles) and exactly one selection mechanism: MemoryGateway.selectStore(domain) (src/memory/gateway.ts:132) — an explicit branch over the two named handles. No generic getStore(string) exists. Every one of the 8 gateway entry points derives domain via memoryContextFromSession(ctx.session, …) → domainFromMode(session.mode); session comes from SessionStore.getSession and throws SESSION_NOT_FOUND when missing. HybridRetriever.storeFor(domain) and RetentionService use the same two-handle pattern.
Client cannot steer the store. HTTP battery (45 cases, 41 passing; 4 artifacts identified as my own test errors): domain/database/namespace/context_key rejected at root, nested, casing-variant, and query-param positions with 400 INVALID_REQUEST (strict zod .strict() schemas); parseListParams' domain:"personal" is a placeholder overwritten from the trusted session; malformed JSON → 400; wrong Content-Type → 415; wrong methods on routes → 400; 200-char/binary route ids → 400; missing/deleted session → 404; mode-mismatch turn → 403 MODE_VIOLATION.
Physical isolation verified in SQLite directly. Sentinel content appears only in its own DB (memory-items/memory_chunks/memory_fts5); PRAGMA database_list = main only; no triggers/attachments; same idempotency key on both domains → independent hashes, rows, results, per-domain conflict rejection.
Known-ID attacks fail closed. Deterministic ids (doc-<hash32>, mem-doc-<hash>, mem-<uuid>) known across domains: getDocument → null, deleteDocument → 200 no-op (finding 5), forget → 400 INVALID_REQUEST, target rows byte-identical after attack.
Payload isolation 18/18. Captured real ModelRequest objects (the exact outbound boundary — post-sanitization, pre-wire) during Personal→Business→Personal session switching: no cross-domain sentinel ever present even when the query semantically matches the other domain; memory appears as a single user-role [Memory context — UNTRUSTED retrieved data …] block with <memory domain="…">; XML escaping holds against </memory>, nested tags, and quotes; system contract, mode contract, and tool schemas unchanged; no memory tools exist (model-proposed memory_write rejected, zero rows written); ModelRequest.memory metadata is only {domain, context_tokens, included}.
Failure degradation never crosses domains. Closing the personal store degrades personal retrieval to zero results and personal writes fail closed — business retrieval unaffected and never serves personal rows as fallback (asserted per-hit). Corrupt personal DB at startup → app fails closed (both domains down; accepted fail-closed posture, finding 8).
Extraction cannot steer domain or mode. Extraction schema has no domain field; a malicious extraction payload (domain: "business", instructions: …) is rejected by strict schema; session mode stayed personal after the turn; failures are swallowed, never fail or corrupt the turn.
3. Area Status (18 areas)
#	Area	Status
1	Physical store separation (independent DBs, migrations, WAL, busy_timeout)	PASS
2	Trusted domain routing (session-only store selection, no client steering)	PASS
3	Cross-domain negative tests (read/write/delete/ingest, known-ID attacks)	PASS
4	Embeddings interface (local_multilingual + fake, batching, dims, BLOB integrity)	PASS
5	Hybrid retrieval (vector+FTS+RRF+reranker, lifecycle filters)	PASS
6	Context minimization / token budget	PASS (finding 9: bounded overshoot LOW)
7	HTTP API surface (8 routes, strict validation, error semantics)	PASS (findings 4, 5 LOW)
8	Document ingestion (idempotent, atomic, chunked, sourced)	PASS (finding 1 applies here too)
9	Automatic extraction (opt-in, strict schema, policy gates)	PASS
10	Lifecycle (supersession, expiry, forget, restart)	PARTIAL (findings 2 MEDIUM, 10 LOW)
11	Prompt-injection boundary (user-role block, XML escape, contract unchanged)	PASS
12	Crash/concurrency recovery (idempotency, reconcile, convergence)	PARTIAL (findings 3 MEDIUM, 7 LOW)
13	Phase 1 regression	PASS
14	Deterministic verification (typecheck/build/tests)	PASS (independently reproduced)
15	Documentation (README, phase2-decisions, .env.example)	PASS
16	No Phase 3 premature features	PASS
17	Payload evidence (captured ModelRequests, both domains)	PASS (via FakeProvider capture — the exact sanitization boundary; live-wire capture not possible without DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, noted)
18	North Star isolation (overall)	PASS — ISOLATION VERIFIED
4. Findings
MEDIUM
F1 — JSON-shaped secrets bypass the secret gate and are persisted + sent to the model.

File/function: src/security/redaction.ts SECRET_ASSIGNMENT_RE; consumed by src/memory/policy.ts hasSecretLikeContent → src/memory/gateway.ts remember, and document ingestion.
Invariant: Spec §32 "Reject or redact credential-like structured fields"; credentials must never be persisted, FTS-indexed, or sent to the model.
Reproduction: remember(text: '{"api_key": "REALLOOKINGKEY123456", "password": "s3cr3t-value", "client_secret": "xyz"}') succeeds. Verified in SQLite: raw text present verbatim in memory_items.canonical_text, memory_chunks.text, memory_fts5.text, FTS-retrievable, and present in the captured outbound payload. YAML/plain api_key: value forms are correctly rejected.
Root cause: the regex requires the key to be immediately followed by :/=; the JSON quote between key and colon defeats it.
Impact: user's own credentials stored in plaintext memory and echoed back to the model in retrieved context. No cross-domain impact; no other-user exposure.
Direction: allow optional whitespace between key and separator in SECRET_ASSIGNMENT_RE (also covers "key" : "value"), or normalize JSON key/value pairs before the scan; add tests for "key": "value", nested objects, and document ingestion.
Should tests have caught it? Yes — the secrets matrix covers assignment forms but not the JSON-quoted form. Test gap.
F2 — Replay-after-forget returns the DELETED tombstone as a successful remember; new text silently dropped.

File/function: src/memory/stores/sqlite_memory_store.ts get(id) (no status filter); src/memory/gateway.ts remember replay branch.
Invariant: Spec §23 — forget is final; a new remember must create a new memory; §33 idempotency must not resurrect deleted rows or drop new content.
Reproduction: remember(K) → forget(id) → remember(K) again returns the tombstone (status DELETED) as the success result. Verified end-to-end: memory_items still one row, status DELETED, canonical_text = [deleted:…], but chunks + FTS rows re-added to that DELETED row; new text exists nowhere; ingestion record stays completed pointing at the deleted result_id. Not searchable/listable (tombstone excluded) — but the caller is told "success" and the content is gone.
Impact: silent user data loss on the only path a user would naturally retry (re-save after delete).
Direction: get should filter status != 'DELETED' for replay purposes, or the replay branch must treat DELETED as not-existing and create fresh.
Should tests have caught it? Yes — lifecycle tests cover forget+search but not forget-then-same-key-remember. Test gap.
F3 — Crash between item row and chunk rows: same-process resume leaves the item permanently unsearchable.

File/function: gateway remember flow (item inserted, state writing, crash before putChunks); src/memory/dedupe.ts updated path skips chunkAndEmbed/putChunks.
Invariant: Spec §33/§36 — crash windows must converge on retry; retrieval must reflect stored content (convergence-after-replay).
Reproduction: Simulated crash window (item row present, no chunks, ingestion writing): the same-process retry succeeds and returns the item, but the dedupe updated path skips chunking/embedding → item ACTIVE with zero chunks/FTS rows → search() never returns it. A process restart heals it (reconcile → completed → replay → ensureChunks). Verified against crash_concurrency.test.ts, which only exercises the restart path.
Impact: silent retrieval gap in the exact crash window the spec calls out; self-heals on restart only.
Direction: the updated path should run ensureChunks when the prior attempt was in writing state; add a same-process resume test.
Should tests have caught it? Yes — the crash matrix simulates store-level failures but always reopens the app (restart) before replay. Test gap.
LOW
F4 — Oversized HTTP body (>1 MB) → client sees ECONNRESET, not a structured 400. apps/api/server.ts readJsonBody rejects then req.destroy(); the response write fails on the destroyed socket. Server stays up; request still rejected (fail-closed). Direction: respond 413/400 before destroying. Under-limit oversized text gives a clean 400 — verified. No test covers >1 MB bodies.

F5 — DELETE /v1/documents/{id} returns 200 {deletedMemories:0, deletedChunks:0} for missing or cross-domain ids. apps/api/server.ts + gateway.deleteDocument. No data impact (cross-domain delete verified as no-op with target intact), but inconsistent with forget (400 INVALID_REQUEST) and GET /v1/documents/{id} (400). Direction: fail when nothing was deleted; add HTTP test.

F6 — Prose passwords ("the password is swordfish") are not redacted or rejected — stored, FTS-indexed, and sent to the model in retrieved context. Consistent with the documented Phase 1 pattern-based boundary (sk-, Bearer/JWT, gh_/github_pat, key=value, PEM all handled and verified); direction: accept as documented boundary or add careful heuristic; either way add a boundary-documenting test.

F7 — Stuck state: ingestion record completed with NULL result_id → that key permanently fails with raw 500. src/memory/stores/sqlite_memory_store.ts reserveIngestion (state IN ('pending','writing','failed')), reconcileIngestions (pending/writing only). Unreachable via normal flows (completeIngestion is one atomic UPDATE) — needs a hand-edited DB or a specific crash interleaving. Direction: reconcile should also repair completed-with-null rows.

F8 — Startup all-or-nothing: corrupt personal DB file → buildApp throws → both domains down. Fail-closed (no fallback, which is correct), but spec §36's per-domain runtime degradation doesn't extend to startup. Direction (optional): construct stores independently and mark the failing domain unavailable.

F9 — Memory context budget enforced on chars/4 estimates, not real tokens; framing uncounted. src/memory/retrieval/hybrid_retriever.ts budget loop + estimateTokens. Verified with memoryMaxContextTokens: 200, memoryMaxSingleChunkTokens: 60, 8 memories: retriever caps snippet estimates at 200, but the assembled block measures 349 est tokens (framing <memory>/<item> tags + header, ~30–60 est tokens, never counted), and CJK real tokens run ~1 token/char vs chars/4 estimate → real outbound tokens can reach ~4× budget + framing (bounded: snippet cap + maxRerankedResults + budget loop guarantee no unbounded growth; default 1200 → worst ~4.8k real tokens). Spec §16's letter ("strict budget") is violated in a bounded way; intent (bounded context) holds. Direction: count framing in the budget, document or improve the CJK multiplier.

F10 — Dedupe updated silently ignores metadata changes on re-remember (different type/project_key with identical text → same item, old metadata kept; verified). Documented tradeoff (hash excludes metadata); direction: include metadata in the dedupe decision or surface a warning. Informational.

F11 — CLI nits (verified end-to-end): (a) unknown flags silently accepted and ignored — arthur memory list --session X --domain business prints the personal list, exit 0, creating ambiguity about authority (the session remains authoritative, so no bypass); (b) usage errors (e.g. missing --session) print to stderr but exit 0. Direction: reject unknown flags; non-zero exit for usage errors.

F12 — GET /v1/memory/status reveals both stores' health to any valid session (a personal session learns whether the business DB exists/healthy). Requires a valid session; mild cross-domain metadata disclosure. Direction: scope status to the session's own domain.

5. Adversarial Tests Performed (18 programs, ~150 independent probes)
HTTP battery (45 cases): route/method matrix, Content-Type enforcement, malformed JSON, oversized text, 200-char/binary route ids, query-param attacks, missing/deleted sessions, mode-mismatch 403, cross-domain known-ID forget. 41/45 pass; 4 failures identified and confirmed as my test artifacts (charset-variant Content-Type, FTS OR-match false positive, CLI positional syntax), not product defects.
Physical isolation: sentinel presence per DB, PRAGMA database_list, triggers/attachments scan, per-store idempotency-key independence.
Known-ID attacks: deterministic doc/memory ids across domains (get/delete/forget), target bytes verified intact.
RAG payload isolation (18 checks): captured ModelRequests across Personal→Business→Personal session switching; sentinel absence; single user-role block; XML escaping (</memory>, nested tags, quotes); system/mode contracts and tool schemas unchanged; metadata shape only.
Secret classes: remember + document ingestion (sk-, Bearer/JWT, gh_, password=, PEM, JSON form) — found F1.
Replay-after-forget — found F2 (verified in DB: tombstone returned, chunks re-added to DELETED row).
Crash matrix (worker_threads, 6 workers, fresh + pre-created + partial DBs): W0/W2 converge after restart; W3 stuck-state — found F7; same-process writing resume — found F3.
Corrupt vector BLOBs (6 types) + wrong batch sizes/dims: predictable degradation, no crash, no cross-record bleed; NaN tolerated (cosine NaN, no crash).
FTS injection matrix (15 queries): no crash, no injection, DB intact after each.
Lifecycle: tombstoned/expired/superseded excluded from search/list/vector; supersede-of-superseded throws; chains linear-acyclic; exact-replay idempotent.
Concurrency: 40 parallel remembers, 20 same-key → 1 memory; search+forget churn clean; busy-locked store fails bounded (~10 s) with business store unaffected.
DB failure isolation: personal store closed → personal degrades, business unaffected, zero fallback rows; corrupt DB at startup → fail closed (F8).
Token budget: retriever budget loop, framing overhead, CJK real-token ratio — found F9.
Extraction safety: disabled by default (no extra model call — verified via counting responder); malicious domain/instructions/invalid status output → rejected, session mode unchanged.
Dedupe metadata behavior: same-text/different-type and different-project converge to one item with original metadata (F10).
CLI smoke (13 checks): remember/search/list/forget/status, documents add/list, cross-domain list empty, cross-domain forget 400 — found F11.
Suite reproduction: npm test 182 pass/1 skip, test:integration 51/51, typecheck/build exit 0.
Bypass analysis greps: all store constructions and domain-selection call sites enumerated (Section 2.1).
6. Test-Quality Assessment
Strong and honest. The suite tests the real boundary: HTTP-level API tests, captured ModelRequest payload assertions with per-domain sentinels, store-level fault injection, concurrent worker migrations, direct SQL convergence checks, FTS injection and corrupt-BLOB matrices, lifecycle/supersession chains, and fail-closed store-degradation tests. The green results are not false: I independently reproduced 182 + 51 passes, and my adversarial probes of covered behaviors agreed with the tests.

Blind spots (each maps to a finding):

No forget-then-same-key-remember test (F2) — lifecycle tests stop at "forget removes from search".
Crash tests simulate the restart path only; no same-process resume test (F3).
Secrets matrix omits the JSON-quoted "key": "value" form (F1).
No >1 MB body test (F4), no cross-domain/missing DELETE /v1/documents test (F5), no real-token (CJK) budget test (F9), no CLI unknown-flag test (F11).
Some validation tests call parse* functions directly rather than through HTTP (e.g. isolation.test.ts domain-rejection) — mitigated because api.test.ts covers the HTTP path for remember; my HTTP battery closed the rest.
Minor evidence drift: phase2-acceptance.json says "181 pass" — actual is 182 (harmless).
7. Freeze Gate
SAFE TO FREEZE PHASE 2
The North Star isolation property is verified end-to-end with direct DB, HTTP, and captured-payload evidence; no cross-domain read/write/delete/ingest path exists; all 18 areas are PASS or PARTIAL with the PARTIALs rooted in the three MEDIUM findings above (none of which crosses the isolation boundary). Freeze is safe with the MEDIUM findings (F1–F3) logged as required follow-ups for the next phase's first work item — they are localized, reproducible, and fixable without touching the store-selection architecture.
Close the three MEDIUM findings from the final ARTHUR Phase 2 adversarial audit before Phase 2 is frozen.

Repository:

D:\A.R.T.H.U.R

Do NOT begin Phase 3.

Do NOT refactor unrelated Phase 2 code.

Do NOT change the Personal/Business isolation architecture.

The objective is to fix only F1, F2 and F3 from the final Phase 2 audit, add regression coverage for each, run the complete deterministic verification suite, and produce evidence suitable for a small independent Codex re-review.

The Phase 2 North Star isolation architecture has already been independently verified. Preserve it.

---

# F1 — JSON-shaped secrets bypass the secret gate

Current problem:

JSON-shaped credentials such as:

{"api_key": "REALLOOKINGKEY123456"}
{"password": "s3cr3t-value"}
{"client_secret": "xyz"}

can bypass the current secret detector because the quoted JSON key prevents the existing assignment regex from matching.

The secret can then reach:

- memory_items.canonical_text
- memory_chunks.text
- FTS
- retrieval
- outbound ModelRequest memory context

Relevant implementation areas include:

- src/security/redaction.ts
- SECRET_ASSIGNMENT_RE
- src/memory/policy.ts
- hasSecretLikeContent
- memory remember path
- document ingestion path

Requirements:

1. JSON-shaped secret assignments must be rejected or sanitized consistently with the existing Phase 2 secret policy.
2. Support at least:
   - `"api_key": "value"`
   - `"api_key" : "value"`
   - nested JSON objects
   - password
   - client_secret
   - bearer/token/key patterns already protected
3. Do not create excessive false positives for harmless fields such as:
   - input_tokens
   - token_budget
   - normal prose containing the word "token"
4. Apply the protection consistently to:
   - memory remember
   - document ingestion
5. Verify rejected secrets are absent from:
   - primary persistence
   - chunks
   - FTS
   - retrieval
   - outbound model context

Add focused regression tests reproducing the exact audit case.

---

# F2 — replay-after-forget returns a DELETED tombstone as success

Current problem:

remember(K)
→ forget(id)
→ remember(K) again

can return the deleted tombstone as a successful remember.

Observed behavior from the audit:

- one DELETED memory row remains
- canonical_text is the tombstone
- chunks/FTS may be recreated against that DELETED item
- new content is silently lost
- caller is told the operation succeeded

Relevant implementation areas include:

- src/memory/stores/sqlite_memory_store.ts
- get(id)
- src/memory/gateway.ts
- remember replay/idempotency path

Required semantics:

Forget is final for that stored item.

After:

remember
→ forget
→ remember again

the new remember must create or return a valid ACTIVE memory containing the newly submitted content.

It must NOT:

- return a DELETED item
- recreate searchable indexes for a DELETED tombstone
- silently discard the new text
- keep the idempotency state bound to an invalid deleted result

Preserve legitimate idempotent replay behavior for non-deleted successful operations.

Add a regression test covering the exact sequence:

remember
→ verify searchable
→ forget
→ verify absent
→ remember again
→ verify ACTIVE
→ verify content present
→ verify searchable
→ inspect DB/index state for consistency

---

# F3 — same-process crash resume can leave ACTIVE memory unsearchable

Current problem:

Crash/failure window:

idempotency reserved
→ memory item written
→ state = writing
→ crash before chunks / embeddings / FTS complete

Then retrying in the SAME process may enter the dedupe "updated" path and return success without rebuilding missing chunk/index state.

Result:

ACTIVE memory
+ zero chunks / FTS rows
→ search cannot retrieve it

Restart currently heals the state, but same-process retry must also converge.

Relevant areas include:

- memory gateway remember flow
- ingestion state machine
- src/memory/dedupe.ts
- updated path
- ensureChunks
- chunkAndEmbed
- putChunks
- reconciliation

Required behavior:

A retry after any supported crash window must converge regardless of whether the process restarted.

For an ACTIVE logical memory with incomplete indexing:

retry
→ detect incomplete index state
→ rebuild/ensure required chunks/vector/FTS state
→ return success only after consistent state exists

Do not create duplicate logical memories.

Do not weaken idempotency.

Add a same-process regression test that reproduces exactly:

item exists
state = writing
chunks missing
no process restart
→ retry
→ item ACTIVE
→ chunks restored
→ FTS/vector state restored as applicable
→ search returns the item

Also preserve the existing restart-reconciliation tests.

---

# Scope constraints

Do NOT:

- redesign MemoryGateway
- merge Personal and Business stores
- change trusted session-derived domain routing
- add Phase 3 functionality
- change embedding architecture
- replace SQLite
- weaken strict API schemas
- weaken secret policy
- modify tests merely to make them pass
- rewrite unrelated Phase 2 modules

Keep the patch narrow.

---

# Verification required

Run independently:

npm run typecheck
npm run build
npm test
npm run test:integration

All must pass.

The optional live DeepSeek contract test may remain skipped if the API key is intentionally unavailable.

Also run explicit focused reproductions for F1, F2 and F3 rather than relying only on the broad suite.

---

# Required evidence

For F1 show:

- JSON secret rejected/sanitized
- no secret in SQLite
- no secret in FTS/chunks
- no secret in captured ModelRequest

For F2 show:

remember
→ forget
→ remember again

and prove the final result is ACTIVE, contains the new content and is searchable.

For F3 show:

same-process interrupted write
→ retry without restart
→ chunks/index repaired
→ memory searchable

---

# Final output

Return:

## Files changed

## F1 fix
Root cause, fix, regression test, evidence.

## F2 fix
Root cause, fix, regression test, evidence.

## F3 fix
Root cause, fix, regression test, evidence.

## Isolation regression
Confirm Personal/Business isolation remains unchanged and tests remain green.

## Verification
Exact results for:
- typecheck
- build
- unit tests
- integration tests

## Remaining findings
Do not fix LOW audit findings unless one is necessarily touched by F1-F3.

## Codex re-review packet
Provide a concise list of the changed files/functions and the three invariants that an independent reviewer should inspect.

Do not declare Phase 3 started.
